assign.outcome:
**All eleven landed, the last one included: the realm now has ONE renderer for a configured page, and the builder's middle column is it.**

![The Code button, at 1280 — the whole page.js, at the top of the rail. It was a 22px strip holding nineteen lines](shots/drawer-code-1280.png)

**The button whose promise got louder while the thing behind it stayed broken.** `pre.code-block` is a flex child of `.drawer-body flex v`, and a `<pre>` scrolls — which makes its automatic minimum height **0**. A flex item that may shrink to nothing does. Both boxes are **291px and 282px** at 1280 now (348 and 338 at 3440), and each scrolls itself.

**A page you made draws its own children.** [`make/notes/`](/imagine/paging/make/notes/) drew *Overview · Pricing · Docs · Contact* — the demo's four samples — with no link to either of its own two children. Its tab strip reads **Today · Later**, each panel carries *"open Later as its own page"* pointing at its real url, and a click still reports **"the box did not move: still 927 × 503px"**.

![A page you made, at 1280 — its own children, and the way to them](shots/made-notes-1280.png)

**"Make this a page" names the page you are making.** It took the title, icon and description of the page you were standing on, so making a page from the hub gave you a second page called *Paging*. Typed `Docs browser` in the drawer's new name field: the JSON changed as I typed, `made/docs-browser/page.json` appeared with my seven words, and the line said **Saved to disk — Open Docs browser**, linking `/imagine/paging/make/docs-browser/`. It opens cold with those words. (Deleted after; `made/` is byte-identical.)

**Build's step 7 prints the seven words**, in the same shape the drawer's does — a `Paging` page with one `this.stage({…})` call. Pressed *Tint* then *Panel right* and the printed file changed with them. `width: "large"` — core's word, which this realm calls **Room** — is gone.

**And Build's blocks reach the page. Decided: drawn, not deleted.** They were collected, saved into `mode.blocks` and read by nothing outside `build/`. One renderer ([`build/draw.js`](/imagine/paging/doc/builder/)), two callers: the builder's middle column, and a made page through the stage's `draw` seam. **The rule: a page draws its blocks if it has any, and the `content` word's sample if it has none.** Proved end to end — added a paragraph in Build, saved, opened the page it wrote, and the paragraph is in the box.

**One name per thing, rail → bar → address.** The bar is built from the **six blocks, in the rail's order**; **SKIN** holds its three under one heading; **Stage** owns none and [its page now says why](/imagine/paging/stage/). The address says the words you see — `?content-colour=tint&page-colour=plain&type-size=compact` — and the old keys are still read, so every saved link opens. [Navigation](/imagine/paging/navigation/) has the bar now too, below its measurements rather than beside them.

**`?nest=` takes any page.** [A page I made, running inside a blog preset](/imagine/paging/library/blog-post/), from `?nest=/imagine/paging/make/<name>/`. And **taking one out can be sent**: `?nest=` empty survives a refresh, because `url.js` now tells *"the address said nothing"* from *"the address said none"*. One more thing that was broken: `?nest=magazine` on the nest preset used to be ignored — the address wins now.

![Cross at 1280 — pick any two of the seven words](shots/cross-1280.png)

**[Cross](/imagine/paging/cross/) is two dropdowns**, not a hard-coded three by three: any word across, any word down, every pair a live page (42 by default). Each cell has a **13rem floor** and the wall scrolls itself — six pages across a 1024px middle is 130px each, and a page in 130px sets one letter per line.

**Make at 3440 and Build at 1280, in numbers.** A page's name sat **2,300px** from its own word chips; it is **7px** now ([picture](shots/make-rows-3440.png)). The builder's card is 957px at 1280, under its 64rem stacking floor, so the live stage landed **2,100px down** on the page whose claim is "the middle column is the page assembling as you click". The floor is 54rem: the stage is **479px down**, three columns, first screen.

![Build at 1280 — three columns, and the middle is a PagingStage](shots/build-1280.png)

**`BuildStage` renders a `PagingStage`.** `build/stage.js` **260 → 98 lines**, `build.css` **−91**: the tab strip, the rail, the sheet, the row list and five surface classes are `paging.css`'s now, drawn once for the builder and for a real page alike. `stage.js` grew three hooks, seven lines together — `draw`, `draw_child`, and `picked` (which child is open, for a caller that rebuilds the stage on every keystroke).

**Checked:** 34 pages × 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440 = **136 loads, zero console errors** (the one line is core's declared-child probe 404 on `readme/page.js`, by design), no sideways scroll. Private server 8099, killed by pid. `made/` byte-identical to where it started.

**Left, deliberately, one thing:** the builder's middle can now wear the realm's own bar in one line, which would give Build the four words it has no control for. It is small, it is written down in [doc/builder.md](/imagine/paging/doc/builder/), and it is a new control rather than a fix.
